title: Platform Mechanics Atlas — Visibility, Persistence, Incentives and Social Memory
purpose: Model a platform as an active mediation system rather than a neutral container. Track how affordances, ranking, identity, monetization, moderation, archive rules and portability change what becomes visible, repeatable and memorable.

questions: Is identity persistent, pseudonymous, verified, portable or disposable?
What can be posted: text, video, live, thread, story, file, reaction, remix?
Follower graph, search, recommendation, trending, embedding, notifications or direct delivery?
Replies, quote-posts, duets, stitches, reactions, chat, moderation, collaboration?
Which signals influence ordering or recommendation?
Which parts are known versus opaque?
Ads, subscriptions, donations, revenue share, commerce, sponsorship, no direct monetization?
Rules, enforcement, appeals, account-level sanctions, object-level sanctions, age gates, regional restrictions?
Searchability, deletion, edit history, caching, clipping, download, external archives, API access?
Can users export identity, content, audience graph, subscriptions or archives?
Which metrics are public, private, estimated, sampled or unavailable?

core_mechanisms.mechanism: Only a subset of available objects is surfaced to a user.
Exposure produces interaction; interaction can affect further exposure.
core_mechanisms.boundary: Observed correlation between engagement and reach does not by itself reveal the full ranking algorithm.

core_mechanisms.mechanism: Material produced for one audience/time can circulate into another context.
Copies, clips, quotes, screenshots and external archives can outlive the original object or account.
A creator/community may depend on platform-owned discovery, payments, identity or audience access.
Rules and enforcement change which practices can persist.
Character limits, clip length, live chat, threading and remix tools change expression and interpretation.
Visible metrics become goals and status signals, changing behavior.

comparison_rule: Compare platforms by mechanisms and measurements, not by vague claims that one platform is 'more free', 'more toxic' or 'more viral'.

handoffs.information_ecology: Translate platform mechanics into attention, memory, repetition and correction dynamics.
handoffs.subculture_group_formation: Pass repeated interaction patterns only when there is evidence of identity, norms, roles or reproduction.
handoffs.witness_attestation: Preserve what was publicly witnessed without inferring private motive.
handoffs.below_observatory: Escalate abuse, harassment or illicit-network questions only with evidence-specific case records.
